The point estimates in the forecast at each horizon—1 day, 1 week, and 1 month—were driven by the underlying trends in the data, as well as expected short-term and medium-term behaviors of the system being modeled. For the 1-day forecast, the estimate of 149.1 relies heavily on recent trends and assumes minimal deviation because of the short time frame. Moving to the 1-week horizon at 149.5, the model anticipates some slight evolution in the observed trend, perhaps accounting for recurring patterns or external influences that typically occur over that timeframe. At the 1-month horizon, the point estimate shifts more substantially to 150.3, reflecting a longer-term view that incorporates a gradual drift in the underlying factors affecting the predicted outcome.

The confidence interval (CI) widths grow wider as the forecast horizon extends, reflecting an increase in uncertainty. For the 1-day horizon, uncertainty is low because short-term trends tend to be more predictable with fewer variables impacting outcomes. By 1 week, the CI widens due to the possibility of more external influences or random fluctuations that could deviate from the trend. Over the 1-month period, the uncertainty becomes much larger (141.2 to 159.4), as there is a greater likelihood of unforeseen events, structural shifts, or more complex interactions in the system, all of which could meaningfully impact the forecast accuracy.

Certain risks or events could push outcomes outside your stated intervals, especially at longer horizons. These might include rare or extreme events, such as economic shocks, policy announcements, market disruptions, or other unexpected developments. If, for example, a sudden external shock introduces a significant deviation from the historical trend or drastically alters the underlying drivers of the forecast, the actual values may fall outside the 90% confidence bounds. While the intervals aim to capture most likely scenarios, they cannot account for every possible contingency, particularly low-probability, high-impact events.
